messages:
Marta (Sales): Heads up — Obelisk Finance wants a POC to replace CompetitorX. Main asks: identical chat outputs for existing prompts, proof of no data exfil, and a pricing comparison for our hosted vs their API. Can we map this out quickly?
Chen (SE): Thanks. I spun up a small bridge proxy to normalize request/response shapes. Main differences so far: CompetitorX uses `stop_sequences` semantics that terminate on any token in a set; our `stop` behaves similarly but there are corner cases with streaming.
Patrick (Presales): Important: Obelisk's product team is strict on prompt parity — they have ~120 golden prompts. We need a test harness and a perf baseline (99th p95 latency under 400ms).
Olivia (SRE): For POC infra I'm +1 on a dedicated dev pool in eu-west-1 (they're EU-only). We'll need IP allowlist, short-lived creds, and logs forwarded to their SIEM.
Kevin (Customer Eng): Also: they bill per-request for us vs per-token for CompetitorX. Need to show cost parity or explain delta. Can we create a sample cost model with realistic token counts?
Chen (SE): I can run the eval harness. Plan: 1) import the 120 prompts, 2) hit both endpoints, 3) compare responses with fuzzy metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, and a custom semantic similarity embedding threshold).
Marta (Sales): Security team asked for KMS/HSM details and an outline for our data retention + deletion flows. SecBot — any quick checklist?
SecBot: Automated security checklist: 
- KMS integration supported (customer-managed keys)
- Audit logs available for all request metadata
- VPC peering and private endpoints for Private deployments
- SOC2 report available on request
Please attach completed questionnaire to this thread. :lock:
Patrick (Presales): For prompt parity, watch out for tokenizer differences — CompetitorX uses byte-level bpe that splits emojis differently. Add a normalization step: 
```
# normalizer pseudocode
text = unicode_normalize(input)
text = replace_emojis_with_aliases(text)
text = collapse_whitespace(text)
```
That fixed a bunch of off-by-one token issues in our last test.
Chen (SE): Noted. Also noticed truncation policy differs: their API truncates to max_tokens="hard" while our runtime returns a 413-like error for oversize. I added a soft-truncation pre-check to the proxy to return `max_tokens` adjusted to available quota.
Marta (Sales): What about hallucination deltas? Obelisk legal wants a statement on regression risk and rollback plan.
Kevin (Customer Eng): We can demo baseline diffs and an automated rollback to CompetitorX fallback for a hybrid deployment if parity fails. They care about no-disruption during fallbacks.
Olivia (SRE): Fallback plan ops notes: route policy -> if mismatch_rate > 15% for 10m then route to fallback model; emit trace with `x-fallthrough-reason`. We'll need a canary toggle in Console.
Patrick (Presales): Pricing model: I'll prepare a 30-day sample bill using their historical traffic (provided by Obelisk) and model two scenarios: (A) Hosted per-token with caching/prefix hints, (B) Dedicated reserved capacity. We should include expected monthly committed spend and peak burst margins.
Marta (Sales): Great. Timeline? Obelisk expects initial POC results in 2 weeks. Who owns what?
Chen (SE): I own the eval harness + proxy normalization. ETA 6 days to run full set.
Patrick (Presales): I'll craft the cost model and presales deck. ETA 3 days.
Olivia (SRE): I'll provision EU dev pool and IPs by EOD tomorrow, and add the log forwarder. Need legal to sign a DPA before we ship logs.
Kevin (Customer Eng): I'll prepare the rollback demo and sample integration guide. ETA 5 days.
Marta (Sales): Security questionnaire: Kevin, can you fill the data flow diagram section? Patrick — add the fallback and SLA notes.
Kevin (Customer Eng): On it.
Chen (SE): Early heads-up: one more compatibility wrinkle — CompetitorX's streaming chunk boundaries include metadata frames; our streaming API strips those. I'll add a small shim to reinsert `meta` frames so their client parser doesn't break. Example shim: 
```
# stream shim pseudo
for frame in our_stream:
  if is_text_frame(frame): yield frame
  else: yield {"meta": frame.meta}
```

Marta (Sales): Perfect. Obelisk also asked about compliance: can we support GDPR data subject requests in the POC?
SecBot: GDPR flow: data access/export and right-to-be-forgotten supported for Private & Dedicated. Hosted has a 30-day retention default but can be reduced for Enterprise with contract addendum.
Patrick (Presales): I'll include a slide that maps each legal ask to an implementation (auditable logs, KMS, DPA clause, retention TTL adjustments).
Olivia (SRE): One blocker: Obelisk requires FIPS 140-2 for crypto in EU deployments. Our Private infra supports FIPS via HSM; Hosted requires an enterprise contract. Flagging this as a potential commercial hold.
Marta (Sales): Noted — I'll raise that in the commercial call.
Chen (SE): Quick troubleshooting note: a couple of prompts show tokenization-induced punctuation shifts leading to small semantic changes. I pushed a normalization patch to the proxy repo `obridge/normalizer:v0.3`. Please pull before running local tests.
Kevin (Customer Eng): Also collecting the golden prompts — Obelisk will send a csv with annotations (expected behavior, allowed variance). Once we get that, I'll upload to the eval harness.
Marta (Sales): Okay team — action items recap: 1) Chen: eval harness + proxy normalization (6d). 2) Patrick: pricing + presales deck (3d). 3) Olivia: EU dev pool + logs (1d). 4) Kevin: rollback demo + questionnaire sections (5d). 5) Marta: commercial call re: FIPS/DPA (ASAP). We aim to present initial findings in 12 business days.
Chen (SE): Sounds good. I'll post a short runbook snippet to this thread after first harness run.
Patrick (Presales): If anyone needs the cost template I used last quarter, ping me — I'll drop it here.
Marta (Sales): Thx everyone. I'll sync with Obelisk and push their connector CSV into the secure drop once received. :rocket:
